name: Comparison
summary: Two to four options side by side: each with its name, price and a Choose button, then one row per attribute so the differences line up.
use: when someone is choosing between a few fares, plans or memberships and wants the differences in one view
a11y: A table with a column header per option and a row header per attribute, so each value is read with both; ticks and crosses are decorative and the value is always in words; each Choose button is named with its option.

use_when: two to four options of the same kind that differ on a few named attributes, such as fare types or plan tiers
avoid_when: more than four options or a long list to browse: use result-list
one item and its details: use product-card
options that only need a name to pick from: use quick-replies

parts.name: note
parts.what: one line of context: route and date, or who it is for

parts.name: badge
parts.what: a short badge on the recommended option, which also gets the accent button

parts.name: price_note
parts.what: what the price covers, such as 'per person'

parts.name: rows
parts.what: one attribute, with a value per option

parts.name: values
parts.what: one value, in the same order as the options

parts.name: value
parts.what: the value in words, with a tick or a cross when it is a yes or no

empty.how: with fewer than two options there is nothing to compare: answer in text, or use product-card for one

loading.how: keep the column headers and fill names, prices and values with muted blocks of their height

error.how: if prices cannot load, leave price out and say why in the note

disabled.how: a Choose button for a sold-out option is disabled and dimmed

overflow.how: on a phone each attribute name moves above its values; four options scroll sideways in their own box

long_text.how: names, values and labels wrap inside their column; the badge stays on one line with an ellipsis

keyboard: Tab moves through the Choose buttons, one per option, left to right
